unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: The analytic zeta package and the critical-line statement
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Representation change and compression: compare the zeta-side analytic package with the xi-side symmetric geometry. The gain is an even entire zero problem with the trivial zeros separated; the limitation is that symmetry is strictly weaker than the conjectured reality statement and removes none of the central proof burden.
unit_index.interpretation: Passing from zeta in the s-plane to the entire even xi function packages the pole-removing and gamma factors and converts the nontrivial-zero question into reality of xi zeros, equivalently critical-line location for nontrivial zeta zeros. This expresses RH inside a symmetric zero problem, but evenness and reflection symmetry organize the zero set without forcing every xi zero to be real.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Weighted prime counts connect analytic counting to exact combinatorial identities
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge object is the weighted count, positioned between primes and a combinatorial factorial identity. Logarithms convert factorial products into additive prime-power contributions, enabling inequalities unavailable in the raw counting representation.
unit_index.interpretation: Weighting is a strategic relaxation: it forgets the equal contribution of each prime but gains compatibility with products and factorials. The resulting representation is easier to bound while retaining enough information to transfer order-of-magnitude control back to ordinary counting.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Zeta is a prototype whose zeros encode global arithmetic objects
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Global L-functions bridge algebraic, arithmetic, and automorphic objects to analytic invariants. Euler factors retain local information, while zeros, poles, and special values provide global summaries from which arithmetic consequences may be extracted.
unit_index.interpretation: The generalization preserves a structural interface rather than one formula: local factorization, global analytic symmetry, and spectral-looking distinguished data. This makes RH one instance of a family-wide decoding problem rather than an isolated zeta phenomenon.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Independent zero counting plus critical-line sign changes certifies a finite RH window
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The contour integral compresses all enclosed zeros and poles into one integer, while xi sign changes localize candidates on the target line. Their equality is the bridge from numerical observations to a finite completeness claim.
unit_index.interpretation: The protocol closes the sampling gap by coupling detection with an independently conserved total. Apparent line zeros alone are incomplete evidence; equality with the global contour count certifies that no additional off-line or higher-multiplicity zeros remain in the bounded region.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: A positive proportion of simple critical-line zeros transfers across major L-function classes
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Evidence-channel separation: contrast counting verified critical-line zeros with bounding possible off-line zeros, and treat the proportion as a coarse population statistic for cross-family comparison. This gains abundance information but loses individual identities and cannot upgrade a positive fraction to all zeros.
unit_index.interpretation: A positive-proportion theorem constrains the zero set from the good side: it establishes that many nontrivial zeta zeros are both simple and on the target line, whereas zero-density estimates constrain possible bad behavior. The similar conclusions reported for named L-function families broaden the phenomenon, but the span does not identify a common proof method or make a uniform claim for every L-function.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: The classical case lacks global analogues of cohomology, Frobenius, and the index theorem
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Cohomology, a Frobenius-like operator, and an index pairing are proposed bridge roles between arithmetic data and zero geometry; the adelic setting is only a possible arena. No actual classical bridge object is supplied in the span.
unit_index.interpretation: The missing objects are functional requirements for a mechanism: a state space carrying zero data, an operator producing spectral parameters, and a pairing theorem enforcing the needed sign. The Maass case is a falsification test for any proposal tied too narrowly to classical geometry.

unit_index.source_title: Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
unit_index.unit_title: Naturality criterion for a Hilbert–Polya realization
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge runs from zeros to an unfolded point process and then to eigenvalues of a natural pair (H,D), with Selberg and function-field analogues supplying precedent.
unit_index.interpretation: Selfadjointness or positivity would relocate RH into operator theory, but the statistical match is primarily a diagnostic for whether the sought representation has the right spectral organization.

unit_index.source_title: Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
unit_index.unit_title: Fourier control of the local fixed-point denominator
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Self-dual additive Fourier transform bridges delta-kernel multiplication to convolution of line measures, identifying the local trace contribution used in Weil's formula.
unit_index.interpretation: The inverse local denominator measures transversality of two linear constraints and survives uniformly across Archimedean and non-Archimedean fields.

unit_index.source_title: Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
unit_index.unit_title: Geometric summability and rapid decay of the cutoff error
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The S-unit logarithmic lattice bridges word length to local magnitude, while fractional-difference Fourier estimates bridge local regularity to decay of the quotient tail.
unit_index.interpretation: The proof separates two burdens—summability over arithmetic translates and cutoff convergence—and supplies a different control mechanism for each.

unit_index.source_title: Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
unit_index.unit_title: The cutoff angle spectrum also governs random-matrix gap probabilities
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge object is the product of a position projection with a Fourier-conjugated projection; its eigenvalue product is a generating function for random-matrix gap counts and its spectrum is related to Theta by the ab scaling invariance.
unit_index.interpretation: Operator angles compress the interaction of two cutoffs into a spectrum that can be reused in a probabilistic eigenvalue-counting formula. The useful move is to compare constructions through a common spectral invariant rather than through their ambient interpretations.

unit_index.source_title: Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
unit_index.unit_title: Zeros characterize the annihilator of the orbit-sum range
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The decisive bridge chain is E-range to annihilator, compact-character decomposition to Mellin distributions, multiplication by L to support at its zeros, and delta derivatives to generalized eigenvectors of the transposed representation.
unit_index.interpretation: The cokernel changes analytic vanishing into linear-algebraic failure of surjectivity. Multiplicity is not merely repeated eigenvalue counting: derivatives supported at a zero supply generalized eigenvectors and hence Jordan structure.

unit_index.source_title: Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
unit_index.unit_title: Poincaré transversality yields periodic-orbit and zero contributions
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The graph delta, diagonal pullback, normal-bundle map, Poincare return map, and pushforward to the time axis form the bridge from flow geometry to periodic-orbit and fixed-zero trace contributions.
unit_index.interpretation: Existence and weight have the same source: the failure of fixed directions transverse to the orbit. Quotienting out the flow direction exposes the Poincare return map, and its determinant measures the density distortion of the graph-diagonal intersection.

unit_index.source_title: A Computational History of Prime Numbers and Riemann Zeros
unit_index.unit_title: From prime tables to a local density heuristic
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Prime indicators are replaced by weights 1/log n and the weighted sum by an integral; this preserves aggregate growth while forgetting exact locations and short-range irregularity.
unit_index.interpretation: A local statistical rule compresses a jagged counting problem into a smooth asymptotic law; the useful object is the density, not a prediction of individual primes.

unit_index.source_title: A Computational History of Prime Numbers and Riemann Zeros
unit_index.unit_title: Weighted prime counts linearize the prime-zero bridge
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Λ records prime powers additively after logarithmic differentiation, and Weil's test functions provide adjustable Fourier bridges between weighted zero sums and weighted prime sums.
unit_index.interpretation: Choosing coordinates adapted to the operative algebra can linearize a difficult relation; direct counting is traded for a weighted object whose analytic transform is simpler.

unit_index.source_title: A Computational History of Prime Numbers and Riemann Zeros
unit_index.unit_title: Counting all zeros is the completeness half of RH computation
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes numerical RH verification into localization and global accounting. The theta term gives a tractable main count and S(T) records the discrepancy needed for an exact total; this gains a completeness audit but loses the nearest-integer simplification when the path or discrepancy conditions fail. The proof burden remains establishing the contour condition and accounting with multiplicity rather than merely finding apparent critical-line roots.
unit_index.interpretation: Locating zeros on the critical line and certifying completeness are different obligations. The all-zero count N(T), counted with multiplicity, supplies an independent total against which the critical-zero count N₀(T) can be checked. Backlund's argument-principle analysis represents N(T) as a theta main term plus the path-integral correction S(T); the correction is not itself the full zero counter. The nearest-integer shortcut is fragile because it requires a suitable nonvanishing contour and a height where the correction is small, while the source says S(T) is unbounded.

unit_index.source_title: A Computational History of Prime Numbers and Riemann Zeros
unit_index.unit_title: Scale, reproducibility, and provenance of zero verifications
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: A finite-height RH claim is represented by a computational record linking software, algorithms, numerical range, and reported result, rather than by the zero count alone.
unit_index.interpretation: Scale and correctness are different axes; confidence in computed mathematical claims also depends on reproducible methods, preserved records, and independent checking.

unit_index.source_title: A Computational History of Prime Numbers and Riemann Zeros
unit_index.unit_title: Formal analytic estimates plus finite L-function verification close Goldbach
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates theorem-producing analytic estimates, a certified finite analytic input, and a standalone finite check of a different conjecture. The combination gains explicit rigor unavailable from an unverified assumption, but finite L-function verification is not promoted to a global RH result and binary enumeration is not confused with a ternary proof. The unresolved proof burden is precisely how Platt's certificates feed Helfgott's estimates.
unit_index.interpretation: The ternary Goldbach result combines distinct kinds of rigor without the span specifying a clean complement-of-ranges mechanism. Helfgott's improved major- and minor-arc estimates yielded the unconditional weak Goldbach theorem, and his proof used Platt's interval-arithmetic verification of RH for a bounded collection and height range of Dirichlet L-functions as a finite analytic input. This shows that certified computation can enter an analytic proof as a rigorously delimited ingredient, but the exact interface between that ingredient and the circle-method estimates remains unstated here.

unit_index.source_title: A Computational History of Prime Numbers and Riemann Zeros
unit_index.unit_title: Slow iterated logarithms defeat finite numerical intuition
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Diagnoses information loss in finite-range representation and turns the warning into a reusable falsification question about observationally compatible asymptotics. Computation retains authority over the finite values it checks but loses the ability, by appearance alone, to distinguish a very slow divergence from bounded behavior. The proof burden for extrapolation remains outside the sampled pattern.
unit_index.interpretation: Finite numerical observation can erase the distinction between boundedness and extremely slow divergence. The witness log log log x is unbounded yet can look bounded on a computer, so a persistent plateau does not preserve the global asymptotic property one may be tempted to infer. The constructive response is counterfactual scale analysis: ask which qualitatively different long-run behaviors remain compatible with the observed range, and require theoretical and heuristic considerations before promoting a numerical pattern to a global conjecture.

unit_index.source_title: A NEW LEHMER PAIR OF ZEROS AND A NEW LOWER BOUND FOR THE DE BRUIJN-NEWMAN CONSTANT
unit_index.unit_title: Heat-deformed cosine transform turns RH into a real-zero condition

unit_index.interpretation: Embedding ξ in H_t reframes a static location-of-zeros assertion as zero geometry attached to a parameterized family. The deformation creates room for later monotonicity and threshold arguments, although those are not yet established here.

unit_index.source_title: A NEW LEHMER PAIR OF ZEROS AND A NEW LOWER BOUND FOR THE DE BRUIJN-NEWMAN CONSTANT
unit_index.unit_title: Lehmer pairs compare a tiny gap with interaction from all other zeros

unit_index.interpretation: The criterion measures whether the close pair is isolated strongly enough relative to the background zero configuration. A tiny local scale alone is insufficient; it must be certified against the full environment.

unit_index.source_title: A NEW LEHMER PAIR OF ZEROS AND A NEW LOWER BOUND FOR THE DE BRUIJN-NEWMAN CONSTANT
unit_index.unit_title: Convert local zero counts into an inverse-square tail bound
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The chain is zero ordinates → unit-bin counts → a weighted series → an integral bound; x_j=2γ_j transfers the result back to H_0's zero representation.
unit_index.interpretation: This is a reusable count-to-mass conversion: local cardinality bounds control a global summable quantity when paired with a decaying weight. It supplies analytic coverage beyond any finite computed window.

unit_index.source_title: A NEW LEHMER PAIR OF ZEROS AND A NEW LOWER BOUND FOR THE DE BRUIJN-NEWMAN CONSTANT
unit_index.unit_title: Bound the finite local block by the two adjacent outer gaps
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The ordering of zeros bridges individual denominators to adjacent-gap bounds, and x=2γ bridges those gaps to the computed ordinate data.
unit_index.interpretation: Ordered real zeros make the nearest admissible outer points worst cases for reciprocal-square distances. This converts a finite but large sum into a count times two boundary contributions.

unit_index.source_title: A NEW LEHMER PAIR OF ZEROS AND A NEW LOWER BOUND FOR THE DE BRUIJN-NEWMAN CONSTANT
unit_index.unit_title: Aggregate the three bounds to certify the close pair as Lehmer
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The sum M+I+R reconstructs the global interaction, while the dimensionless gap-interaction product bridges that global bound to Definition 1.1's Lehmer certificate.
unit_index.interpretation: The proof is modular: separate conservative controls can be aggregated because the final admissibility test depends only on their total and the local gap. The large slack makes the classification robust to modest looseness in the background estimate.

unit_index.source_title: A NEW LEHMER PAIR OF ZEROS AND A NEW LOWER BOUND FOR THE DE BRUIJN-NEWMAN CONSTANT
unit_index.unit_title: Explicit error absorption proves the unit-interval zero-count certificate
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The decomposition N=s+e bridges a global main term plus error to a unit-step count; the α and β inequalities bridge heterogeneous lower-order terms to a common log T budget used by the tail argument.
unit_index.interpretation: An asymptotic counting formula becomes a uniform local statement through explicit error absorption. The proof exposes how a threshold is chosen so lower-order terms fit inside the slack left beneath the target coefficient of log T.

unit_index.unit_title: Finite-height role of classical zero-free regions
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Writing each region as a height-dependent deficit from σ=1 makes the finite-height comparison a comparison of boundary widths and connects it to explicit prime-distribution applications.
unit_index.interpretation: A stronger asymptotic rate need not dominate at computationally or arithmetically relevant scales, so optimizing the constant in a nominally weaker form remains meaningful.

unit_index.unit_title: Improved zero-free and Landau bounds
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The admissible classes Pₙ and their limiting infimum connect finite polynomial witnesses to a global upper bound on V, while the analytic machinery connects a selected witness to the zero-free region.
unit_index.interpretation: A certificate can be evaluated through different transfer maps: one yields a zeta zero-free constant, while another yields an extremal-polynomial bound, and the two achievements should not be conflated.

unit_index.source_title: Nonnegative trigonometric polynomials and a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: Split the eta range and balance complementary denominator bounds
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The auxiliary cutoff η₁ is a balancing variable joining height information, kernel monotonicity, and retained error sign into a minimax computation.
unit_index.interpretation: A coarse global relaxation is repaired by partitioning the uncertainty domain and matching complementary local bounds at their bottleneck.

unit_index.source_title: Nonnegative trigonometric polynomials and a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: C4: isolate numerically tractable middle ranges and analytically bound tails
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The breakpoints t*, ±1/2, and b(1±ε) are proof-relevant intermediate objects that turn a difficult whole-line integral into separately controllable obligations.
unit_index.interpretation: Partitioning aligns each subdomain with the strongest available representation: symmetry, the correct branch of a piecewise majorant, local numerics near a peak, or closed-form tail decay.

unit_index.source_title: Nonnegative trigonometric polynomials and a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: Refined annealing yields the degree-40 Landau certificate
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Changes the epistemic object from a successful stochastic run to a proposed finite inequality witness, while making the witness claim conditional on verification of its explicit data rather than importing a certification protocol.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: after degree-by-degree searches produced a degree-40 polynomial with V_40<34.48923, finer annealing passes produced F_40, whose evaluated objective is reported to give V_40<34.488992000856 and hence the paper's upper bound for V; coefficient data are placed in figures. Conceptual interpretation: the search trajectory is heuristic, whereas a fixed admissible polynomial can serve as a finite witness for an upper bound on an infimum once its coefficients and objective value are verified. This gains a reusable witness rather than reliance on the optimizer's path, but the present prose span does not expose enough coefficient or rounding evidence to make independent numerical certification checkable. Global optimality and any lower bound remain outside the claim.

unit_index.source_title: Nonnegative trigonometric polynomials and a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: Zero-free width propagates to explicit prime-counting error bounds
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Builds a dependency map from the upstream region constant to multiple downstream bounds and distinguishes asymptotic equivalence of boundary representations from equality of their finite explicit consequences.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: the improved zero-free region is inserted into cited prior arguments to obtain revised explicit bounds for theta and psi with R=6.315 and for pi-li with leading constant 0.2593; the source also says that a shifted-log zero-free region, although asymptotically equivalent to the analyzed form, could further improve these finite corollaries. Conceptual interpretation: the zero-free constant functions as an upstream quantitative interface: changing it permits several downstream estimates to be updated by controlled substitutions rather than by rederiving all cited arguments. The gain is reuse and propagation across prime-counting quantities; the loss is that this span is not self-contained and its finite constants still depend on the hypotheses, thresholds, and cited arguments. Exact formulas remain extraction-sensitive.

unit_index.source_title: On the roots of the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: Finite critical-line verification as a bounded computational claim
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The critical-line representation and the ordering of zeros by height turn a global location conjecture into a finite certification problem with an explicit cutoff.
unit_index.interpretation: This is finite exhaustion within an ordered range, not induction from examples: the force of the result comes from claiming that every zero up to the cutoff has been accounted for.

unit_index.source_title: On the roots of the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: Riemann-Siegel compression of critical-line evaluation
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: A phase factor produces a real auxiliary function on the critical line, and a finite cosine-type sum plus controlled remainder bridges zeta values to tractable sign computations.
unit_index.interpretation: The gain is representational compression rather than a new conjectural principle: a complex critical-line evaluation is converted into a short real oscillatory sum whose signs are usable for root detection.

unit_index.source_title: On the roots of the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: Remainder-aware screening and local refinement of exceptional intervals
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Gram-point values, a Riemann-Siegel remainder bound, coded flags, and a finer local mesh form a bridge from approximate evaluation to interval-level root-count evidence.
unit_index.interpretation: The key move is certified abstention followed by adaptive refinement. Error bounds do not merely assess final accuracy; they decide which observations count as signs and where more computation is required.

unit_index.source_title: On the roots of the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: Increasing failure frequency with nearly balanced displacement direction
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Cumulative counts and block increments compress many interval-level events into a trend, while the right-left split retains orientation information lost by the total alone.
unit_index.interpretation: Increasing local unreliability of the one-root heuristic does not by itself create a directional drift. Rate and direction are distinct statistics of the displacement process.

unit_index.source_title: On the roots of the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: From frequency anomalies to low-amplitude extrema and close roots
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Viewing the real critical-line function continuously inside each Gram interval connects root spacing, intervening extrema, and the mesh resolution needed for reliable detection.
unit_index.interpretation: Amplitude is a conditioning variable for root detection. Two distinct roots can become hard to certify not because the counting principle changes, but because the sign margin between them is exceptionally small.

unit_index.source_title: On the roots of the Riemann zeta-function
unit_index.unit_title: Additional 15,000-root computation
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Hold the undefined qualitative descriptor apart from the precise finite-location observation and identify coexistence, rather than silently converting "worse" into Gram-law irregularity or into evidence against RH.
unit_index.interpretation: The addendum extends the finite experiment to the next 15,000 roots and records two coexisting observations: the zeta-function's behavior became steadily "worse" in an undefined qualitative sense, yet every examined root still had real part one half. The useful distinction is that qualitative deterioration in some observed behavior does not by itself negate the reported finite critical-line result. This comparison gains an evidential guardrail against conflating the two statements, but loses any more specific diagnosis because the note supplies neither a definition of "worse" nor a detailed method, height cutoff, simplicity claim, or global implication.

unit_index.source_title: Bounds for discriminants and related estimates for class numbers, regulators and zeros of zeta functions : a survey of recent results
unit_index.unit_title: Eliminate inaccessible constants, then enforce sign control
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Compares successive representations by the work each makes possible: constant elimination enables an initial estimate, differentiation enables stronger combinations, and explicit formulas improve the bound while exposing the analytic constraints. This preserves the distinction between an established methodological gain and mechanisms hidden by the defective formula extraction.
unit_index.interpretation: The analytic progression changes which parts of the discriminant argument are tractable: Stark first eliminates two hard constants from a Hadamard-factorization identity, then combines the prime-ideal expansion valid for real s>1 with a specialization of s to obtain estimates; later differentiated identities strengthen the bounds, and the Guinand-Weil explicit-formula presentation both improves the GRH result and makes the method's requirements and limitations clearer, with subsequent unconditional extensions. The gain is a more effective and auditable analytic interface, while the proof burden remains in the missing identities, parameter choices, and estimates; the surviving prose does not justify reconstructing cancellation or positivity mechanisms.

unit_index.source_title: Bounds for discriminants and related estimates for class numbers, regulators and zeros of zeta functions : a survey of recent results
unit_index.unit_title: Prescribed local completions unify discriminant and curve-genus minimization
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge objects are prescribed local completions; archimedean signatures instantiate the number-field side, while finite-field point conditions and genus instantiate the curve side.
unit_index.interpretation: The global quantity is studied relative to a local specification rather than in isolation. This reframing exposes a reusable constrained-minimization pattern shared by number fields and curves while allowing the invariant and local conditions to change with the category.

unit_index.source_title: Bounds for discriminants and related estimates for class numbers, regulators and zeros of zeta functions : a survey of recent results
unit_index.unit_title: Infinite class-field towers defeat divergence of minimal root discriminants
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Hilbert class field towers bridge ramification behavior to asymptotic degree families; root discriminant is the tower-stable statistic that makes the contradiction visible.
unit_index.interpretation: A tower is a counterexample generator: repeated degree growth combined with invariant root discriminant invalidates a global growth expectation. The useful obstruction is structural rather than a single exceptional numerical field.

unit_index.source_title: Bounds for discriminants and related estimates for class numbers, regulators and zeros of zeta functions : a survey of recent results
unit_index.unit_title: Tailor kernels to known, absent, or targeted small prime ideals
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Contrasts general-purpose optimization with evidence-conditioned kernel selection and identifies the representational tradeoff: a kernel strong without auxiliary information may suppress the moderate-norm contributions one wants to use, whereas a tailored kernel makes specified presence, absence, or emphasis operational in the global estimate.
unit_index.interpretation: Kernel design should depend on the arithmetic information available. Kernels optimized for discriminant bounds with no prime-ideal information decay rapidly and may be nonmonotone, so they can underuse known ideals of moderate norm; the alternative explicit-formula construction permits termwise comparison, strengthens the stated estimate when norm-2 prime ideals are absent, and can be redesigned to emphasize particular ideals. The gain is an evidence-conditioned probe rather than a universally optimal bound, and the proof burden remains in verifying the missing kernel, inequalities, and admissibility conditions.

unit_index.source_title: Bounds for discriminants and related estimates for class numbers, regulators and zeros of zeta functions : a survey of recent results
unit_index.unit_title: Ideal-class zeta functions improve Minkowski constants but resist GRH import
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Ideal-class zeta functions bridge analytic estimates to class-wise small ideals; the different and class inversion organize the paired alternative, while the induced discriminant inequality is a coarser consequence.
unit_index.interpretation: The analytic representation preserves ideal-class information that a bare discriminant bound loses, but that gain changes the available structure: without an Euler product or valid GRH, familiar conditional machinery cannot be transferred by analogy. Representation choice trades one kind of information for another.

unit_index.source_title: Bounds for discriminants and related estimates for class numbers, regulators and zeros of zeta functions : a survey of recent results
unit_index.unit_title: Use the same kernel to compare prime and zero shares, then test kernel sensitivity
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Treats the table as a case-specific accounting control and the unconditional-kernel comparison as a sensitivity analysis. This separates a valid within-case residual decomposition from an invalid fixed-kernel comparison across cases and identifies kernel choice as part of the attribution mechanism.
unit_index.interpretation: For each of six selected fields, the GRH-bound kernel chosen for that case supplies one coherent accounting identity: deficiency is compared with the computed prime-ideal contribution, and the zero contribution is obtained as the residual. The scale parameter b varies across degree/signature cases, so the controlled comparison is within a row rather than under one fixed kernel across the panel. The reported comparable shares are therefore panel- and representation-dependent; rerunning the accounting with the best unconditional kernel makes the zero share considerably larger relative to the prime share, demonstrating kernel sensitivity rather than an intrinsic universal balance.

unit_index.unit_title: Assemble the corollary from spectral truncation and mean-value control
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates pointwise asymptotic extraction from family-level error transport and identifies the spectral mean value as the mechanism joining them. It also distinguishes two independent closure burdens, discrete and continuous, rather than treating localization alone as the end of the proof.
